newsitem.title: USA: New heart-shaped speed pills found in drug bust.
newsitem.headline: New heart-shaped speed pills found in drug bust.

text.p: A new form of speed -- small, pink heart-shaped pills -- was discovered on Friday in a drug seizure in the Texas border town of El Paso, officials said.

U.S. Customs Service spokesman Roger Maier said police found hundreds of thousands of the pink pills inside a car during a search on the bridge that crosses the border from Ciudad Juarez in Mexico to El Paso.
"I've never seen anything like it," Maier said. "Thousands of pink little heart pills. No one even knew what it was at first."

The pills were found by a drug-sniffing dog inside the car's dashboard. Police arrested the car's driver, a Mexican citizen, and chemical tests later identified the pills as amphetamines, more commonly known as speed.
Maier said raw chemicals used to make amphetamines were often seized along the U.S.-Mexico border, but rarely already-prepared pills.
Drug Enforcement Administration officials said amphetamines were becoming increasingly popular in the United States, and that more and more amphetamine labs were springing up in Mexico.
